beginner.headline: Tomorrow (Wed Oct 14): conditional for beginners; lower confidence than a same-morning report, and your morning on-site check decides. SSW swell slowly easing, now about 12 s (NWS); models have Canoes around 2.5–3 ft. ENE trades 10–15 kt after a breezier night. Best 7–10 AM, just after the 6:23 AM high (2.1 ft) and before trades fill in.
beginner.recommendation: Plan for 7–10 AM: the tide falls from the 6:23 AM high (2.1 ft) toward the 1:47 PM low (0.6 ft), so the reef has the most water early, and trades are forecast lightest early (model about 10 mph NE, gusts 15). Watch several full set cycles first: the swell is easing, but 12 s sets still run above the average and reach further inside. ENE trades are cross-offshore at Waikīkī, so expect seaward drift, more from late morning. The DOH list was not read, so check water color at Canoes and toward the Kūhiō drains and Ala Wai side; brown, gray or cloudy water ends it. One student or a small group of strong adults; several students or children only if sets stay small and drift is low. Your on-site read overrides this report.

water.headline: DOH advisory list not read this run; water quality at Canoes not verified
water.statement: No DOH water-quality list (brown water, bacteria, sewage) could be read this evening, so nothing can be said about Waikīkī, Oʻahu or statewide notices for Wednesday. The last list read (Mon morning) had none for Waikīkī and one open at Bellows–Sherwood (windward Oʻahu); that has not been re-verified. Not finding an advisory does not prove the water is clean. Check water color.
water.why: The DOH Clean Water Branch home page lists no specific advisories and points to the eha-cloud live list, which could not be fetched this run (third run in a row). News searches found no new Waikīkī or Oʻahu notice in October (a Kauaʻi brown-water advisory was reported Oct 3; current status not verified). Dry, stable weather is forecast Wednesday, which lowers runoff risk but proves nothing.
water.runoff: Brown, gray, cloudy or turbid water, or visible runoff: don't go in, advisory or not. DOH guidance: storm runoff can carry sewage and pathogens; coastal water usually needs about 48 hours to flush.
